notes.findability: Straightforward page nouns and search help, but record sections slide out of view on phones and settings lack a shared local navigation.
notes.density: Desktop cards often hold little data, while large phone introductions and stacked counters delay actual records.
notes.capability: Original detail tabs, export actions and filters are visible in places; collection view/selection tools and deep phone navigation are much less exposed.
notes.aiwork: Research and Queue mention AI activity, but author, timestamp and recorded-model provenance are largely absent from the visible record overviews.
notes.hierarchy: Several routes prioritize promotional headings and summary tiles over the evidence, work item or editable content.
notes.typography: The serif titles establish archival character, but oversized phone headings and faint secondary metadata weaken sustained scanning.
notes.iconography: Consistent outline symbols help navigation, although repeated generic book/location tiles communicate less than the later dossier art.
notes.spacing: Clean alignment is undermined by deep padded cards, nested containers and especially tall mobile summary stacks.
notes.colour: Light parchment and rust are coherent; dark Home/People leave near-black headings and Filter text on dark backgrounds with white cards.
notes.consistency: Collection, record and settings structures vary considerably; dark rendering visibly follows incomplete rules.
notes.fit: Evidence gaps and publication warnings support responsible genealogy, but the visible workspace feels more like a collection of landing pages than a research desk.
notes.cost: Mostly text, small icons and no visible media overhead; production transfer, hydration and infrastructure cost remain unmeasured.

notes.findability: Saved views, search, counted sections and labelled dossier links make desktop discovery strong; phone settings tabs and generic Options still need decoding.
notes.density: Tables and audit rows reveal substantial real information, but mobile introductions/control stacks and some narrow desktop descriptions consume too much height.
notes.capability: Visible grouping, sorting, selection, Table/List/Grid and counted All menus improve reachability; below-crop settings controls and original-detail depth cannot be verified here.
notes.aiwork: Dated evidence streams distinguish You/Your AI, explicitly qualify self-reported models, and expose story authorship and Queue actors without inventing certainty.
notes.hierarchy: Clear page identity, dossier/evidence split and review warnings work well; phone records and Queue still place substantial introductory material before useful work.
notes.typography: Editorial serif titles, restrained body copy and compact metadata form a deliberate ladder, with a few overly long lines and undersized ledger details.
notes.iconography: Code-native dossier/map artwork supplies specific archival identity without pretending to be a portrait or evidence image; small utility symbols remain consistent.
notes.spacing: Desktop collection grids and dossiers align well; phone summaries, repeated preambles and controls need a tighter vertical rhythm.
notes.colour: Parchment, teal and rust carry meaning and the shown dark pages remain legible; settings' orange active navigation is a small cross-surface inconsistency.
notes.consistency: Collection and dossier systems are recognizable across routes, though settings navigation and several title weights retain a separate visual dialect.
notes.fit: The visible evidence, uncertainty, provenance and publication gates feel appropriate for a private genealogy workspace shared with AIs.
notes.cost: Small code-native art and text-heavy layouts appear restrained; no production transfer, first-load or runtime cost measurement supports a higher claim.

notes.findability: Explicit Issues navigation, query, status counts and labelled facets expose the primary collection tools together.
notes.density: Many issues remain distinguishable through consistent title/metadata rows and quiet right-aligned activity.
notes.capability: Views, filters, sorting, layout choices and pagination are visible for the issue collection; authenticated operations are not proven.
notes.aiwork: No automated-work provenance is presented in the reference page; neutral score per brief.
notes.hierarchy: Repository, current Issues surface, query and results have predictable levels; the pinned issue adds modest competition.
notes.typography: Bold row titles and muted metadata are efficient, although the small secondary text is demanding.
notes.iconography: Status, comments, linked work and avatars are consistently positioned and semantically useful.
notes.spacing: Compact aligned rows and economical controls preserve a large working area.
notes.colour: Restrained neutral surfaces and status/label accents support scanning with little decorative load.
notes.consistency: Repeated rows, chips and controls are exceptionally systematic across the shown long collection.
notes.fit: A mature, practical issue desk that makes sustained scanning and filtering credible.
notes.cost: Tiny avatars/icons and no visible heavy media; client payload and infrastructure remain unmeasured.

notes.findability: Plain named groups and descriptive links help genealogists; the search limitation is useful but distant from the search box.
notes.density: Numerous resources fit into meaningful groups, although the sidebar and promotional modules compete.
notes.capability: Research entry points, record types, tools, events and further learning are exposed with substantial navigation depth.
notes.aiwork: No AI or automated work is shown; neutral score per brief.
notes.hierarchy: Group headings organize the directory, but closure notice, news and campaign cards create multiple competing starts.
notes.typography: Readable conventional typography has too many heading treatments and relatively small body links.
notes.iconography: Mixed clip-art, historical thumbnails and promotional graphics have visibly inconsistent styles.
notes.spacing: The main resource grid is coherent; sidebar modules and lower campaign tiles produce uneven rhythm.
notes.colour: Mostly legible institutional colour, with unrelated multicolour navigation gradients reducing unity.
notes.consistency: Box styles repeat, but imagery and module headings belong to several visual systems.
notes.fit: Clear institutional genealogy language and links convey practical authority despite dated presentation.
notes.cost: Several raster/promotional images are visible; no heavy video is apparent and actual delivery cost is unknown.

notes.findability: A numbered linked contents panel, breadcrumbs and explicit access modes make a deep research guide navigable.
notes.density: Guide text, contents and assistance are well grouped, though three narrow columns cause considerable wrapping.
notes.capability: Fifteen contents links, record access methods, advice and related guides expose substantial research depth.
notes.aiwork: No AI or automated work is shown; neutral score per brief.
notes.hierarchy: The guide structure is explicit, but the large cookie/header region delays it and advice competes with the introduction.
notes.typography: Numbered headings are distinctive and body text is readable, with cramped narrow-column line lengths.
notes.iconography: Actual archival imagery is relevant and captioned; contact/access illustrations are less stylistically unified.
notes.spacing: Consistent dividers and column alignment organize depth, but the introductory three-column layout is compressed.
notes.colour: Restrained blue links and neutral guide panels preserve legibility and institutional identity.
notes.consistency: Numbering, links and separators repeat reliably with a few legacy-looking widgets.
notes.fit: Source-specific explanation, archival reference caption and access guidance suit careful family-history research.
notes.cost: One meaningful source image and otherwise mostly text; actual production transfer and script cost are unmeasured.

capabilityConcerns.what: Later record tabs extend beyond the right edge and there is no complete section chooser in the shown crop; the destinations may exist but require more discovery.
Table/List/Grid, saved-view, sort, columns, density and selection tools are not exposed in the shown collection; cannot establish whether available elsewhere.
Actual connection-specific narrowing, end-date and revoke controls are below the required crop; reachability is unproven, not evidence of removal.
Desktop Table/List/Grid and Manage views are not directly visible on phone; Options may retain them but its name does not establish that path.
Phone Contents and original-detail access are below the crop; the tall dossier makes evidence navigation harder to reach even though the desktop counted All 9 menu is visible.
V1 shows three Priority Gaps while this overview shows two; the third may be retained in a deeper section. The crop does not prove its one-step full-detail reachability.
The current operator-ledger destination is off the visible settings navigation strip; its content exists but the active location is harder to identify.
The ledger-first ordering leaves mint/secret/preset forms below the crop; no removal is established, but retaining a labelled jump to creation would make depth clearer.
Narrow/end-date/revoke controls are below this top crop; desktop shows them clearly, but phone action parity and named revoke confirmation cannot be proven visually.
Your data supplies a plausible depth link, but the contents/readers/duration/control comparison and remaining legacy controls are not shown and cannot be scored as verified.

fixes.where: Page titles, explanatory text, Filter button and white collection surfaces
fixes.problem: Dark backgrounds retain nearly black title/button text and unrelated bright white content cards.
fixes.fix: Apply a complete dark surface/text palette: pale foreground for titles and controls, readable muted copy, dark cards and visible separators; keep rust for warnings.

fixes.where: Introductory cards and stacked numeric summaries
fixes.problem: The crop contains mostly preamble and oversized counters; the underlying work is delayed by multiple screenfuls.
fixes.fix: Remove the outer hero-card padding, use a short route title, retain explanatory text at body size, and lay counters into a compact two-column grid with 12–16px cell padding.

fixes.where: Record section navigation below identity card
fixes.problem: A wide strip exposes only the first few phone sections and does not show their counts or a complete section chooser.
fixes.fix: Keep the tabs but add the existing section counts and an always-visible All sections control; put a labelled Contents list directly below the phone identity summary.

fixes.where: Collection header between title and results
fixes.problem: Visible collections expose inconsistent controls and little indication of alternate views, density, grouping or selection.
fixes.fix: Use one collection toolbar that visibly exposes available saved views, search/facets, sort/group, Table/List/Grid and selection; keep every currently available filter and detail link.

fixes.where: Research entries and record overview
fixes.problem: Visible text does not readily show who recorded each update or when; the story header lacks clear authorship/provenance.
fixes.fix: Present existing attribution and timestamps alongside each research entry, and existing recorded-model/unknown-author information in the story summary; label unknowns plainly.

fixes.where: Story identity, workflow step cards and editor
fixes.problem: A long action/step presentation dominates the record before its draft text or evidence.
fixes.fix: Reduce Draft/Review/Published to a compact horizontal step strip, keep the blocker summary adjacent to review actions, and bring the existing draft preview/editor directly below.

fixes.where: Individual place/writing cards
fixes.problem: Large repeated icons, padding and stat tiles consume space without aiding comparison.
fixes.fix: Use a compact list/table presentation with icon, title, status and existing counts on aligned rows; keep the card view available as an alternate.

fixes.where: Permission catalogue preceding actual connections
fixes.problem: The permission explanations dominate the first view and do not reveal which connection currently has which abilities.
fixes.fix: Put existing connections and their allowed abilities together first; retain every full permission explanation in the labelled Permissions section and keep narrow/end-date/revoke controls adjacent to each connection.

fixes.where: Top of settings pages
fixes.problem: Generic Settings, API Center and Admin API lack a common local wayfinding system.
fixes.fix: Add a shared labelled local navigation for AI connections, Preferences & data, Developer keys and the gated operator ledger; preserve the current forms and role boundaries.

fixes.where: Secondary counts, import dates and all-caps metric labels
fixes.problem: Very faint small metadata makes the most useful comparison details harder to read.
fixes.fix: Raise muted text contrast, set desktop metadata to at least 12px with clear line height, and use sentence-case labels for numerical summaries.

fixes.where: Phone dossier card before Contents/evidence
fixes.problem: The complete desktop sidebar becomes a tall phone block; person and story crops end before the evidence/navigation work surface.
fixes.fix: Keep name, key dates/status and critical warning expanded, move the existing Contents control immediately after them, and place secondary operational/provenance fields into labelled compact disclosure groups without removing any fields.

fixes.where: Phone introduction, saved views and toolbar above first result
fixes.problem: Large preambles, multiple control rows and wide vertical gaps consume most or all of the crop before useful work.
fixes.fix: At phone widths use a 28–30px route title, 12–16px section gaps and compact explanatory text; reduce repeated preamble spacing and keep saved-view/search controls directly above the first record. Retain all text and controls through clearly labelled disclosures where needed.

fixes.where: Settings top navigation and AI subsection navigation
fixes.problem: Developer keys is clipped and the operator ledger's active tab is outside the shown horizontal strip; Manual brief also clips.
fixes.fix: Use a wrapping two-column settings navigation or a labelled section selector that always displays the current full section name; retain all destinations and show the active AI subsection clearly.

fixes.where: Search row and generic Options button
fixes.problem: The narrow search placeholder truncates the search scope and Options does not reveal where view/density/columns live.
fixes.fix: Place the search field on a full-width phone row with a persistent Search label, then Search/Filter controls below; label the existing options entry View & columns or display its current view/density summary.

fixes.where: Recently touched tray and phone top actions
fixes.problem: The desktop tray stretches below its last record, while phone title/actions/tray heading consume a large area before the first record.
fixes.fix: Let Recently touched size to its four rows instead of matching the adjacent tray's height; reduce tray description spacing and use one primary phone action plus two compact secondary links while keeping all three destinations.

fixes.where: Story preview paragraph in first list entry
fixes.problem: The preview spans nearly the entire content width, making a long dense line; the same warning is repeated in metadata and again below.
fixes.fix: Limit preview prose to about 75–85 characters per line and put existing review metadata/actions in the remaining side area; show the warning count once prominently while retaining the full warning details.

fixes.where: Task/directive descriptive column
fixes.problem: The first descriptive column wraps short explanations into many lines while secondary scalar columns reserve large widths.
fixes.fix: Give task/directive title and description about 40–45% of the table, tighten priority/state/actor columns to their contents, and keep dates/scalars aligned; retain every column via column settings.

fixes.where: Ledger metadata, connection details and provenance sidebars
fixes.problem: Several long operational details are noticeably smaller than the surrounding working text.
fixes.fix: Increase these details to a consistent 12–13px desktop size, shorten line lengths with wrapping, and keep the qualifying labels attached to their values.

fixes.where: Sidebar Settings active item
fixes.problem: Settings uses an orange filled active item while other active destinations use teal with a rust edge.
fixes.fix: Use the same teal active destination treatment for Settings; reserve rust for warnings, conflict and destructive-action emphasis.

fixes.where: Explanatory copy before first connection/key controls
fixes.problem: The first connection abilities or key actions arrive very low despite the user entering an operational settings surface.
fixes.fix: Present the existing top safety/setup explanation as a compact labelled summary with expandable full text; place current connections/keys immediately after the route heading and keep all scope, expiry and revoke controls within each record.

keep.what: Plain genealogical nouns, visible search and direct links to source people.
The parchment background, editorial serif headings and rust warning vocabulary.
Visible publication blocker count and distinct Draft/Review/Published stages.
Research task descriptions preserve uncertainty and tell the person what to compare.
Original context-pack/JSON actions and detailed legacy settings remain visibly represented.
Counted All section menus, dossier identity and dated evidence streams with You/Your AI attribution.
Explicit unknown/unverified authorship, recorded-model qualification and unresolved evidence wording.
Shared collection saved views, search, grouping, sorting, selection and Table/List/Grid controls.
Connection-by-ability matrix, visible narrow/end-date/revoke actions and current-vault key-ledger boundaries.
Legible shown dark modes, quiet archival SVG placeholders and compact linked Audit numbers without fabricated time trends.

result.summary: V2 is a strong desktop research workspace, with much clearer evidence provenance and collection capability than V1. GitHub remains visibly better at economical scanning and control-to-result distance; V2's largest remaining gap is the amount of phone screen occupied before records, evidence, questions and security actions appear. This judges only the 16 shown route families plus Home/People dark pairs, not the unfinished site or authenticated operation.

pick.label: V2
pick.why: Build V2: its dossiers, collection controls, evidence attribution and coherent dark palette are visibly stronger. Retain V1's direct context-pack/JSON and legacy form discoverability within clearly labelled depth, and borrow the references' economical rows and explicit numbered contents rather than their visual styling.
